chunks: Friendship cannot come to be except by its limits. So whoever has in him these limits, or something of them, then ascribe to him friendship; and whoever does not have in him anything of them, do not ascribe to him anything of friendship.

The first of these is that his private and public behaviour toward you should be one and the same; the second is that he sees your honour as his honour and your fault as his fault; the third is that neither authority nor wealth should change him toward you; the fourth is that he does not deprive you of anything that his capacity can attain; and the fifth — which encompasses all of these qualities — is that he does not abandon you during calamities.

key_terms.الحُدُود: Limits/conditions — the defining criteria that constitute true friendship
key_terms.الصَّدَاقَة: Friendship (sadaqa) — genuine, deep companionship, distinguished from superficial acquaintance
key_terms.النَّكَبَات: Calamities, reversals of fortune — the ultimate test of true friendship
key_terms.زَيْن/شَيْن: Honour and fault — one who regards your glory as his and your trouble as his own
key_terms.سَرِيرَة: Innermost state, private behaviour — what one conceals from others
key_terms.عَلَانِيَة: Public behaviour, outward conduct — what one displays openly
key_terms.وِلَايَة: Authority, position of power — a test of loyalty when social status changes

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions of true friendship according to Imam al-Sadiq in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides a detailed ethical framework for recognising true friendship, enumerating five binding conditions that distinguish genuine friends from mere acquaintances. These criteria — consistency of private and public conduct, shared fortune and misfortune, steadfastness despite changes in power or wealth, generosity within one's means, and loyalty in times of hardship — were addressed to followers in a society where social bonds were often tested by political pressure and material gain. The fifth condition is identified as the supreme test, encompassing all the others.
